canonical_statement: World War II was one war fought by the United States in the 1900s.
linked_questions: Name one war fought by the United States in the 1900s.
curation_rationale: Most iconic and memorable of the five accepted wars. Reinforces rather than duplicates fact 106 (why the U.S. entered WWII) — naming a war and explaining why the U.S. joined it are different cognitive tasks even when they're about the same conflict.

canonical_statement: The United States entered World War I after Germany attacked U.S. civilian ships.
linked_questions: Why did the United States enter World War I?
curation_rationale: Most concrete and specific of the three accepted answers.

canonical_statement: The 19th Amendment (1920) gave all women the right to vote.
linked_questions: When did all women get the right to vote?
curation_rationale: Most specific and memorable — named amendment plus date, distinct from the 15th Amendment (fact 98) it's easy to confuse it with.
visual_treatment: Numeric badge — deliberately visually distinct from the '15' badge used for fact 98.

canonical_statement: The Great Depression was the longest economic recession in modern history.
accepted_answer_variants: Longest economic recession in modern history
curated_answer: The longest economic recession in modern history
visual_treatment: Reuses the dollar-bill icon for economic content.

canonical_statement: The Great Depression started with the stock market crash of 1929.
linked_questions: When did the Great Depression start?

canonical_statement: Franklin Roosevelt was president during the Great Depression and World War II.
linked_questions: Who was president during the Great Depression and World War II?

canonical_statement: The United States entered World War II after Japan attacked Pearl Harbor.
linked_questions: Why did the United States enter World War II?
curation_rationale: Most concrete and iconic of the three accepted answers.

canonical_statement: Dwight Eisenhower signed the Federal-Aid Highway Act of 1956, creating the Interstate System.
linked_questions: Dwight Eisenhower is famous for many things. Name one.
accepted_answer_variants: President during (at the end of) the Korean War
Signed the Federal-Aid Highway Act of 1956
curated_answer: Signed the Federal-Aid Highway Act (Interstate System)
curation_rationale: Chosen deliberately over 'WWII general' — that would sit too close to the many other WWII facts already in the book. The Interstate System is distinctive and concrete.

canonical_statement: The Soviet Union (USSR) was the United States' main rival during the Cold War.
linked_questions: Who was the United States' main rival during the Cold War?
curation_rationale: Most historically accurate/complete of the three accepted terms.
visual_treatment: Balance scale — an ideological standoff, part of the same visual family as other 'opposing forces' facts.

canonical_statement: Communism was one main concern of the United States during the Cold War.
linked_questions: During the Cold War, what was one main concern of the United States?
curation_rationale: More iconic of the two accepted answers, and sets up facts 110's shared answer naturally.

canonical_statement: The United States entered the Korean War and the Vietnam War to stop the spread of communism.
linked_questions: Why did the United States enter the Korean War?
Why did the United States enter the Vietnam War?
accepted_answer_variants: To stop the spread of communism
curated_answer: To stop the spread of communism
curation_rationale: Questions 110 and 111 both resolve to the identical answer — the third Question merge found in this project (after the Declaration and Civil War merges). Same underlying reasoning applied to two different wars.

canonical_statement: The civil rights movement fought to end racial discrimination.
linked_questions: What did the civil rights movement do?
visual_treatment: Plain, respectful treatment given the subject matter.

canonical_statement: Martin Luther King, Jr. is known for fighting for civil rights.
linked_questions: Martin Luther King, Jr. is famous for many things. Name one.
accepted_answer_variants: Worked for equality for all Americans
Worked to ensure people would not be judged by the color of their skin
curation_rationale: Matches the founder's original 'Voices of Equality' deck asset, which paired MLK with Susan B. Anthony (fact 99) directly — recreated here as a real cluster rather than just a visual echo.
visual_treatment: Same people-cluster icon as fact 99, paired in the 'voices_of_equality' cluster.

canonical_statement: The United States entered the Persian Gulf War to force the Iraqi military from Kuwait.
linked_questions: Why did the United States enter the Persian Gulf War?
accepted_answer_variants: To force the Iraqi military from Kuwait
curated_answer: To force the Iraqi military from Kuwait

canonical_statement: On September 11, 2001, terrorists attacked the United States, crashing planes into the World Trade Center, the Pentagon, and a field in Pennsylvania.
linked_questions: What major event happened on September 11, 2001 in the United States?
accepted_answer_variants: Terrorists crashed planes into the World Trade Center
Terrorists crashed a plane into the Pentagon
A plane crashed in a field in Pennsylvania
curation_rationale: Only accepted answer given as a summary rather than the more graphic specific-target variants.
visual_treatment: No icon at all — same treatment as fact 75 (enslaved Africans). This is real, significant trauma for many readers; plain stated text is the right default, not a decorative symbol.

canonical_statement: The war in Afghanistan was one U.S. military conflict after the September 11, 2001 attacks.
linked_questions: Name one U.S. military conflict after the September 11, 2001 attacks.
curation_rationale: Most specific and well-known. Judgment call, worth naming: this fact keeps its icon (unlike fact 115) because it's naming a conflict in the same shape as other 'name one war' facts elsewhere in the book, not depicting the attack itself — a difference of degree from 115, not an inconsistent rule.
